articleTitle: Experiences with an industrially sponsored project course
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Twenty-Second Annual conference Frontiers in Education
abstract: We described a long-running senior design team project. The program provides students with experience in solving a real-world, industrial design problem, working as part of an engineering design team, and communicating the results of their work in written and oral form. Students learn first-hand the engineering design process. We view the course as a critical component of our curriculum. It provides a contextural framework within which engineering courses can be placed. The interdisciplinary nature of the course requires students to integrate the wide spectrum of material they have learned over several years. Of course, as faculty our emotions are mixed in response to proclamations of "AHA! So that's what fluids was all about!" We have observed that the expenence otten dramatically increases students' self-confidence. They obtain a clearer picture of how they can contribute to the engineering design process, and can view themselves as contributing members of an engineering team.
